title: Lawn Stripes
statementMd:
Lawn stripes are drawn using a roller to flatten grass blades in a particular direction and impart a sheen that, at a distance, is distinguishable from blades flattened in another direction. This is typically for aesthetic appeal.

We are going to draw lawn stripes in our square garden using a roller in any of the 44 cardinal directions. The roller must stay on the lawn throughout. The final direction of a piece of lawn is determined by the last time the roller ran over it, including starting from or finishing there.

![image](https://espresso.codeforces.com/0c59cb4dd8a836bce2ea2d189da04ab804bf5c02.png)Illustration of Sample Input 1.

Given a description of the lawn and the starting point of the roller, determine how to draw the pattern.

## Input

- The first line of input contains the width and depth in metres of the lawn, n𝑛 (1≤n≤1001≤𝑛≤100)
- The second line of input contains the row and column of the roller, r𝑟 and c𝑐 (1≤r,c≤n1≤𝑟,𝑐≤𝑛).
- Each of the next n𝑛 lines contains n𝑛 characters from `(l|r|u|d)` giving the desired direction of a square metre of lawn.

## Output

If it is not possible to draw the pattern, output `impossible`. Otherwise, demonstrate a solution in under 10n210𝑛2 moves by outputting the number of moves to use on one line, followed by the moves on the remaining lines.

Each move consists of a distance in metres d𝑑 and a direction from `(l|r|u|d)`. A roller following the instructions must roll over every square metre without leaving the lawn.

samples.output:
8
3 l
3 r
3 d
3 l
1 u
